questions.name: Chikki Pieces: are the six pieces equal?
questions.q_figure: A whole chikki drawn as a rectangle of 24 equal small squares, 6 across and 4 down, shown twice: once cut into six rectangles of 2 squares by 2 squares, and once cut with slanted lines into six pieces that include a triangle.
questions.s_figure: The same two cuttings with one rectangle piece and one triangle piece shaded, each covering 4 small squares' worth.

questions.q_figure: A whole chikki drawn as a rectangle of 24 equal small squares, 6 across and 4 down, and eight separate pieces a to h drawn on the same small squares: a small rectangle, a large right-angled triangle, a flatter right-angled triangle, a tall thin rectangle, an L-shaped piece, a triangle with a vertical side and its tip to the right, a single small square and a small thin right-angled triangle, each with an empty box beside it.
questions.s_figure: The same eight pieces each marked with the number of small squares it covers (2, 6, 3, 4, 3, 4, 1, 1) and its fraction of the whole chikki.

questions.name: Folding a Strip: eighths
questions.q_figure: A paper strip folded into 8 equal parts, with nested brackets under it for 1 part, 2 times 1/8, and so on up to 8 times 1/8, each bracket with empty boxes to fill and the last one reading 8 times 1/8 = 8/8 = 1.
questions.s_figure: The same strip with every box filled: 1/8, 2/8, 3/8, 4/8, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8 and 8/8 = 1.

questions.q_figure: Four circles in a row, each cut into equal parts with one part shaded: the first into 8 parts, the second into 6, the third into 3 and the fourth into 5, with the fractional units 1/3, 1/5, 1/8 and 1/6 written in a row above them.
questions.s_figure: Each circle joined to its fractional unit: the 8-part circle to 1/8, the 6-part circle to 1/6, the 3-part circle to 1/3 and the 5-part circle to 1/5.

questions.name: Number Line: blue line in thirds
questions.q_figure: A number line from 0 to 2 with the unit from 0 to 1 divided into three equal parts, the first mark labelled 1/3, and a blue line from 0 to the second mark with an empty box under its end.
questions.s_figure: The same number line with the blue line shown as two parts of 1/3 each, its end labelled 2/3.

questions.name: Number Line: blue lines in fifths
questions.q_figure: A number line from 0 to 2 with each unit divided into five equal parts, the marks 1/5 and 3/5 labelled, and two blue lines from 0: a shorter one ending at the second mark and a longer one ending at the fourth mark, each with an empty box under its end.
questions.s_figure: The same number line with the two blue line ends labelled 2/5 and 4/5.

questions.name: Number Line: marks in eighths
questions.s_figure: A number line from 0 to 1 divided into eight equal parts with the marks labelled 1/8, 2/8, 3/8, 4/8, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8 and 8/8.
A number line from 0 to 1 divided into ten equal parts, with lines drawn from 0 to 1/10, from 0 to 3/10 and from 0 to 4/5.

questions.q_figure: A number line from 0 to 2 with the unit from 0 to 1 divided into two equal parts, a blue line from 0 to the mark 1/2, and a longer black line from 0 ending halfway between 1 and 2 with an empty box under its end.
questions.s_figure: The same number line with the black line marked as 3 parts of 1/2 each, its end labelled 3/2.

questions.q_figure: A number line from 0 to 2 with each unit divided into five equal parts, the marks 1/5, 2/5, 3/5 and 4/5 labelled, and four black lines from 0 ending at the four marks after 1, each with an empty box under its end.
questions.s_figure: The same four black lines with their ends labelled 6/5, 7/5, 8/5 and 9/5 from the shortest to the longest.

questions.name: Fraction Wall: are 1/2 and 3/6 equal?
questions.q_figure: A fraction wall for one unit: a top bar for 1 unit and below it five rows cut into halves, thirds, fourths, fifths and sixths, every row as long as the top bar and each piece labelled with its fraction.
questions.s_figure: The same wall with the 1/2 piece and the 3/6 piece outlined so that both end at the same place.

questions.name: Fraction Wall: are 2/3 and 4/6 equivalent?
questions.q_figure: A fraction wall for one unit: a top bar for 1 unit and below it five rows cut into halves, thirds, fourths, fifths and sixths, every row as long as the top bar and each piece labelled with its fraction.
questions.s_figure: The same wall with the 2/3 length and the 4/6 length outlined so that both end at the same place.

questions.name: Fraction Wall: sixths that make 1/2
questions.q_figure: A fraction wall for one unit: a top bar for 1 unit and below it five rows cut into halves, thirds, fourths, fifths and sixths, every row as long as the top bar and each piece labelled with its fraction.
questions.s_figure: The same wall with the 1/2 piece and the three 1/6 pieces under it outlined.

questions.name: Fraction Wall: sixths that make 1/3
questions.q_figure: A fraction wall for one unit: a top bar for 1 unit and below it five rows cut into halves, thirds, fourths, fifths and sixths, every row as long as the top bar and each piece labelled with its fraction.
questions.s_figure: The same wall with the 1/3 piece and the two 1/6 pieces under it outlined.

questions.q_figure: Three round rotis, each cut into 4 equal quarters, drawn above four children.
questions.s_figure: The twelve quarters shared out so that each of the four children has 3 quarters.

questions.name: Equivalent Fractions: rotis shared among children
questions.q_figure: Three pictures of rotis shared among children: 2 rotis each cut in half for 3 children, 4 rotis each cut in half for 6 children, and 6 rotis each cut in half for 9 children, with an empty box under every child to write the share.
questions.s_figure: The same pictures with every box showing the share: 2/3 in the first, 4/6 in the second and 6/9 in the third.

questions.s_figure: A number line from 0 to 2 with each unit divided into seven equal steps, a jump of 6 steps of 1/7 starting at 4/7 and landing at 10/7.
